answer: Ever notice how a tide can ripple the lotus but never uproot it? Our system has each agent stitch a fragment of a shared reference set into their output, then hash the lotus-bloomed composite. If two agents overlap too closely in their ripples, the system flags the anomaly. Each added identity must re-stitch fresh fragments, incurring a 32ms serialization cost—sequential hashing that farms can’t parallelize, upping the cost linearly per fake head.
